chunks: Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Fuzayl ibn Uthman, from Ibn Abi Ya'fur, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the word of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'He is the First and the Last' (57:3), and I said: 'As for the First, we have recognised it, but as for the Last, clarify its interpretation for us.'

So he said: 'There is nothing that does not perish, or change, or into which change and decline enters, or that transfers from one colour to another, from one form to another, from one attribute to another, and from increase to decrease and from decrease to increase — except the Lord of the worlds. For He has never ceased nor will He cease to be in one state. He is the First before everything, and He is the Last in the same manner as He always has been.'

Attributes and names do not vary upon Him as they vary upon others — like the human being who at one time is dust, at another time is flesh and blood, and at yet another time is decaying remains and bones; and like the date which at one time is raw, at another time half-ripe, at another ripe, and yet another a dried date — so the names and attributes change upon it. But God, Majestic and Mighty, is the opposite of that.

key_terms.التَّغَيُّرُ وَالزَّوَالُ: al-taghayur wa al-zawal — change and decline/cessation; the defining characteristics of created existence
key_terms.الْآخِرُ: al-Akhir — the Last; divine name indicating God's permanence after all creation with no end
key_terms.الْأَوَّلُ: al-Awwal — the First; divine name indicating God's priority before all existence with no beginning
key_terms.بِحَالَةٍ وَاحِدَةٍ: bi-halatin wahidatin — in one/a single state; God's absolute immutability and unchangeability
key_terms.يَبِيدُ: yabidu — perishes, is annihilated; referring to the inevitable end of created things

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say about the meaning of God being 'the Last' (al-Akhir) in Quran 57:3?
ai.summary: Ibn Abi Ya'fur, one of Imam al-Sadiq's most trusted companions, asked about the meaning of God's name 'al-Akhir' (the Last) from Quran 57:3. The Imam (AS) explained it through a contrast with created things: everything in creation is subject to perishing, change, fluctuation, and alteration of attributes. God alone remains in a single unchanging state — He is first before all things and last as He has always been, without any variation in His divine names and attributes. To illustrate the difference, the Imam used the vivid analogies of the human lifecycle (from dust to flesh to decaying bones) and the ripening stages of a date fruit. This hadith belongs to the theological discussions on divine attributes ('ilm al-asma'), emphasizing God's absolute immutability as distinct from temporal creation.
